observation.visible_scene: A still, low-light landscape: a single leafless tree stands as a dark silhouette on a thin, low horizon ridge. Above it is a smooth sky gradient from deep blue-black at the top (dotted with faint stars) to a pale glow behind the tree. Below the ridge lies a flat, mirror-calm water surface that reflects the tree and the sky glow. The composition is centered and unchanged throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The tree and its mirrored reflection keep the same position, size and outline from the first to the last frame; there is no translation, growth or collapse of the tree.

The water surface shows very slight, slow rippling: the edges and inner detail of the tree's reflection shimmer and warp subtly from frame to frame, indicating gentle surface movement rather than a change in the tree itself.

Small bright specks (particles/snow-like motes) drift slowly across the lower half of the frame, most noticeably a faint point on the right side of the water that shifts position between frames (e.g. brighter/visible around frames 7, 10, 14, 22, 26, 30, 32, 39, 41) and a dim point in the lower-left early on.
The starry sky and overall exposure remain essentially constant; no object enters or leaves the scene, and the horizon line stays at the same height.
The camera framing is effectively static: the tree stays centered and the horizon stays at a fixed vertical position, so the visible motion is object/surface motion, not panning.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the drifting specks are snow, dust or lens/scene noise, and their source or fate beyond the crop.
What causes the faint water ripples (wind, current, etc.).
Any larger camera movement or scene change before t=0 or after t=2.667s, since both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
uncertain_details: A possible very slight vertical drift or distortion of the dark horizon band (a touch thicker on the right in later frames) is at the limit of compression noise and cannot be confirmed as camera motion.
Minor frame-to-frame brightness differences in the sky glow may be encoding artifacts rather than a real lighting change.
Exact identity and three-dimensional trajectory of the bright specks cannot be determined from 2D frames.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
